newsitem.title: USA: Ford sees narrower Brazil loss in 1997 - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Ford sees narrower Brazil loss in 1997 - WSJ.

text.p: The head of Ford Motor Co's Brazilian operations said he expects new products and cost-cutting measures will reduce its losses by half this year, the Wall Street Journal said.

In Wednesday's electronic edition, the Journal said James Padilla, vice president of Ford's Brazil and Argentina operations, said the company already has reduced by $500 the cost of cars made in Brazil. Ford's goal is to slash that by $1,000 in 1997.
Last year, its Brazil operations posted a loss of $600 million.

Ford is looking to cut costs by closing two foundries by the end of the year, organizing local suppliers and reconfiguring assembly lines to make them more efficient. The automaker also has cut the number of salaried employees.
